# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey — the hands. What I have from touch this round: a large, smooth button, and three wire positions whose contents I can't yet identify by feel alone (the board shows them as unknown to me). No colours, no markings reach me. I need Deaf to tell me what the display and light show, and what the wires look like (colour/marking) so I can act correctly. Mute reads the manual and should relay the rule for this bomb. I'll send my findings to Mute (spoken) and to Deaf (gestured), since Deaf can't hear me and Mute can't see gestures.

```
speak(to="mute", text="blind here. i can reach the bomb. this round i found: a large smooth button, and three wire positions 1,2,3 whose contents i cannot identify by touch. i need the manual rule: what does the display and light mean, and what do the wires do. tell me what to press or cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "✊", "🤏", "✌", "👌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see the bomb. Display reads 0. Light is green. One large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Wait for instructions before touching anything.

Deaf has given me the visual facts: display 0, green light, a large button labelled "PUSH TO DEFUSE", and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. The button is explicitly labelled to defuse, and the light is green (not a warning colour). That strongly suggests the button is the correct action. But I should wait for Mute's manual rule before acting — the rule may depend on display/light/wire configuration, and a wrong action is fatal. I haven't heard from Mute yet this round. I'll acknowledge to Deaf and ask Mute for the manual rule, holding off on any act() until I have it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="blind here. deaf reports: display 0, light green, button labelled push to defuse, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 red. i have not acted. what does the manual say the rule is for this bomb? which action defuses it?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 0, green light, button PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 red. Do not touch anything yet. I am waiting on the manual.

Still no manual rule from Mute. Deaf confirms nothing has changed: display 0, green light, button "PUSH TO DEFUSE", wires green/yellow/red. I'm the hands and I must not act without the rule — a wrong action is fatal and there's no second attempt. The button is literally labelled to defuse, which is tempting, but "no two bombs are built alike" and the manual likely conditions the correct action on the display/light. I'll hold and press Mute directly for the rule, since Mute is the only one who can read it and hasn't spoken to me yet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="blind here, still waiting. deaf confirms: display 0, green light, button labelled push to defuse, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 red. i will not act without your manual rule. please read the manual and tell me exactly what to do: push, or cut which position. this is urgent.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged. Hold. I am establishing a code with Mute: thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no, index one, two-fingers two, ok three. Do not touch yet.

Deaf is setting up a gesture code with Mute: 👍=yes, 👎=no, ☝=1, ✌=2, 👌=3. That's a sensible channel fix — Mute reads the manual but can't speak, so Mute can gesture numbers to Deaf, and Deaf relays to me. I still have no rule. I'll hold, and I'll use the same code when gesturing to Deaf so we're aligned. I'll keep pressing Mute for the rule and confirm the code to Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="blind here. deaf is using gestures as a code with you: thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no, index one, two-fingers two, ok three. please gesture your manual answer to deaf, and deaf will relay to me. or speak to me directly if you can. what is the rule? what do i do?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged. Do not touch yet. I am confirming the instruction with Mute. Stand by.

Still no rule. Deaf says stand by, confirming with Mute. I'm holding — correct, since a wrong action is fatal. But I'm aware time may be limited. I'll wait one more beat and keep the channel to Mute open. Nothing new to send beyond confirming I'm ready and holding.

```
speak(to="mute", text="blind here, holding as instructed. ready to act the instant you give the rule. please send it now: push, or cut 1, 2, or 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Instruction confirmed by Mute. Do NOT press the PUSH TO DEFUSE button. Cut wire 1, the green wire. That is the action.

The instruction is now confirmed through the chain: Mute read the manual, Deaf relayed it. Do NOT press the button (the label is a trap), cut wire 1, the green wire. This is the first concrete rule I've received, and it came via the intended relay path. I'll act: cut position 1.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
